top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks with Katori and Ye is a mature, independently reproduced achievement with a clean two-name allocation. The decisive contribution is the magic-wavelength lattice, which allows many atoms to be interrogated at once with the light shift cancelled, bringing optical frequency standards to the 1e-18 level. A citation anchored on that scheme stays separable from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. All eight members support it, and I see no scientific reason to prefer no award, although the early priority record (Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto and others) should be checked.
recusal_note: Doctoral-period research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder (2005 prize context) and neighbouring atomic-physics and quantum-technology fields (Lund colleagues, WACQT, Deep Light Vision); no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye, so no specific recusal conflict apparent from profile.
